question: Apart from nucleus of the cell, which two cell organelles have their own DNA and Ribosomes?
solution:
The correct answer is **'__Plastids and Mitochondria__'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Apart from the nucleus of the cell, the two cell organelles, **Plastids and Mitochondria** have their own **DNA and Ribosomes**
 
• They are **able to synthesize some of their own protein and replicate independently of the nucleus**.
 
• They are also known as autonomous organelles** of cells**.
 
• They are **evolved from bacteria that were engulfed by nucleated ancestral cells, t**hus having their own genomes and their own **biosynthetic machinery** for making RNA and organelle proteins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In most **eukaryotic species, mitochondria are double membrane-bound organelles** and are referred to as the **"powerhouse of the cell"**. They are **located inside the cytoplasm** and effectively serve as the cell's digestive system.
 
• The** plastid is an organelle that is membrane-bound **and is **found in the cells of plants, algae,** and certain other eukaryotic species, 
 
• Most cells include an organelle called the** Golgi apparatus**, sometimes known as **Golgi bodies**. It **performs a crucial function in the secretory process by encapsulating proteins into vesicles before secretion**.
 
• **Animal cells commonly contain lysosomes**, which are membrane-bound organelles. These are** globular vesicles that contain hydrolytic enzymes that can break down a wide range of biomolecules**.
